claim: Classical monocytes give rise to vasculature-resident cells that patrol the luminal side of the endothelium in steady state.
source: In steady state, classical monocytes give rise to vasculature-resident cells that patrol the luminal side of the endothelium.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as an established fact about monocyte behavior in steady state conditions.

claim: Classical monocytes feed macrophage compartments of selected organs including barrier tissues such as the skin and intestine, as well as the heart.
source: In addition, classical monocytes feed macrophage compartments of selected organs, including barrier tissues, such as the skin and intestine, as well as the heart.
evidence: This is stated in the abstract as established knowledge about monocyte contribution to tissue macrophages.

claim: Monocyte differentiation under conditions of inflammation has been studied in considerable detail.
source: Monocyte differentiation under conditions of inflammation has been studied in considerable detail.
evidence: This is a statement about the state of the field, indicating existing research on inflammatory monocyte differentiation.

claim: Monocyte differentiation under non-inflammatory conditions remains less well understood.
source: In contrast, monocyte differentiation under non-inflammatory conditions remains less well understood.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in knowledge that motivates the current study.

claim: Comparison of monocyte differentiation into the colon and ileum-resident macrophages revealed the graduated acquisition of gut segment-specific gene expression signatures.
source: Moreover, comparison of monocyte differentiation into the colon and ileum-resident macrophages revealed the graduated acquisition of gut segment-specific gene expression signatures.
evidence: This is a primary finding of the study based on transcriptomic analysis of engrafted cells.

claim: Embryonic tissue macrophages first develop from primitive macrophage progenitors that originate in the yolk sac in the mouse.
source: In the mouse, embryonic tissue macrophages first develop from primitive macrophage progenitors that originate in the yolk sac (YS).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about macrophage development.

claim: YS-macrophage-derived macrophages persist throughout adulthood in the brain.
source: In the brain, YS-macrophage-derived macrophages persist throughout adulthood, while in most other tissues these cells are replaced by fetal monocytes that derive from multi-potent erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMP).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about tissue-specific macrophage maintenance.

claim: In most tissues other than brain, YS-macrophage-derived cells are replaced by fetal monocytes that derive from multi-potent erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMP).
source: In the brain, YS-macrophage-derived macrophages persist throughout adulthood, while in most other tissues these cells are replaced by fetal monocytes that derive from multi-potent erythro-myeloid progenitors (EMP).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about macrophage replacement in tissues.

claim: Definitive hematopoiesis commences from E10.5 with the generation of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC).
source: Definitive hematopoiesis commences from E10.5 with the generation of hematopoietic stem cells (HSC) that first also locate to the fetal liver, but eventually seed the bone marrow (BM) to maintain adult hematopoiesis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about developmental hematopoiesis.

claim: Most EMP-derived tissue macrophage compartments persevere throughout adulthood without major input from HSC-derived cells.
source: Most EMP-derived tissue macrophage compartments persevere throughout adulthood without major input from HSC-derived cells; however, in certain barrier tissues, as well as selected other organs, like the heart, embryonic macrophages are progressively replaced by HSC-derived cells involving a blood monocyte intermediate (Varol et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: In certain barrier tissues and selected other organs like the heart, embryonic macrophages are progressively replaced by HSC-derived cells involving a blood monocyte intermediate.
source: Most EMP-derived tissue macrophage compartments persevere throughout adulthood without major input from HSC-derived cells; however, in certain barrier tissues, as well as selected other organs, like the heart, embryonic macrophages are progressively replaced by HSC-derived cells involving a blood monocyte intermediate (Varol et al., 2015).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Murine classical Ly6C+ monocytes have a limited half-life once in the blood.
source: Once in the blood, murine classical Ly6C+ monocytes have a limited half-life (Yona et al., 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Ly6C+ monocytes can be rapidly recruited to sites of injury and challenge on demand.
source: On demand, Ly6C+ monocytes can be rapidly recruited to sites of injury and challenge, where they complement tissue-resident macrophages and dendritic cells.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about monocyte function.

claim: In absence of challenge, some Ly6C+ monocytes give rise to vasculature-resident Ly6C- cells which patrol the vessel walls.
source: In absence of challenge, some Ly6C+ monocytes give rise to vasculature-resident Ly6C- cells, which patrol the vessel walls (Auffray et al., 2007).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Vasculature-resident Ly6C- cells display macrophage characteristics including extended life spans.
source: These cells display macrophage characteristics including extended life spans (Yona et al., 2013; Mildner et al., 2017).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior work.

claim: Ly6C+ monocytes replenish selected steady state tissue macrophage compartments including the gut and skin.
source: In addition, Ly6C+ monocytes replenish the above-mentioned selected steady state tissue macrophage compartments, including the gut and skin (Ginhoux and Jung, 2014).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Gut macrophages reside in the connective tissue underlying the gut epithelium, the lamina propria.
source: Gut macrophages, which reside in the connective tissue underlying the gut epithelium, the lamina propria, are considered key players for the maintenance of intestinal homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gut macrophage location.

claim: Gut macrophages are considered key players for the maintenance of intestinal homeostasis.
source: Gut macrophages, which reside in the connective tissue underlying the gut epithelium, the lamina propria, are considered key players for the maintenance of intestinal homeostasis.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge about gut macrophage function.

claim: Monocyte-derived lamina propria macrophages comprise in mice two populations: short-lived cells and long-lived cells with self-renewing capacity.
source: Recent studies revealed that monocyte-derived lamina propria macrophages comprise in mice two populations, that is short-lived cells and long-lived cells with self-renewing capacity (Shaw et al., 2018)
evidence: This is stated as recent knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: The long-lived lamina propria macrophage population might include remnants of embryonic populations.
source: Recent studies revealed that monocyte-derived lamina propria macrophages comprise in mice two populations, that is short-lived cells and long-lived cells with self-renewing capacity (Shaw et al., 2018); the latter population might also include remnants of embryonic populations, as could additional intestinal long-lived macrophage populations that reside near blood vessels, nerves and in the Peyer's Patches (De Schepper et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as a possibility based on cited work.

claim: Additional intestinal long-lived macrophage populations reside near blood vessels, nerves and in the Peyer's Patches.
source: Recent studies revealed that monocyte-derived lamina propria macrophages comprise in mice two populations, that is short-lived cells and long-lived cells with self-renewing capacity (Shaw et al., 2018); the latter population might also include remnants of embryonic populations, as could additional intestinal long-lived macrophage populations that reside near blood vessels, nerves and in the Peyer's Patches (De Schepper et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Evidence for macrophages with different half-lives is emerging for the human small intestine.
source: Evidence for macrophages with different half-lives is also emerging for the human small intestine (Bujko et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as emerging knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Monocyte differentiation into intestinal macrophages involves phenotypic changes with respect to Ly6C, CD64 and MHCII expression, a sequence described as 'monocyte waterfall'.
source: Monocyte differentiation into intestinal macrophages involves phenotypic changes with respect to Ly6C, CD64 and MHCII expression, a sequence described as 'monocyte waterfall' (Tamoutounour et al., 2012).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Mature steady-state gut macrophages tolerate the commensal microbiota and food antigens.
source: Mature steady-state gut macrophages tolerate the commensal microbiota and food antigens (Bain and Mowat, 2011; Zigmond and Jung, 2013).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior work.

claim: The relative unresponsiveness of gut macrophages is thought to rely on regulatory circuits that balance the expression of pro- and anti-inflammatory gene products.
source: Their relative unresponsiveness is thought to rely on regulatory circuits that balance the expression of pro- and anti-inflammatory gene products, such as cytokines and molecules participating in pattern recognition receptor signaling cascades.
evidence: This is stated as a hypothesis about the mechanism of gut macrophage tolerance.

claim: Macrophages located in different tissues display characteristic enhancer landscapes and gene expression profiles.
source: Macrophages located in different tissues display characteristic enhancer landscapes and gene expression profiles, which have been attributed to the exposure of instructing factors of the microenvironment they reside in Amit et al. (2016).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Gut segments display distinct anatomy, function and microbiota load.
source: Gut segments display distinct anatomy, function and microbiota load (Mowat and Agace, 2014)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Macrophages of small and large intestine likely differ.
source: Gut segments display distinct anatomy, function and microbiota load (Mowat and Agace, 2014) and macrophages of small and large intestine hence also likely differ.
evidence: This is stated as an inference based on the differences in gut segments.

claim: The colon and ileum display distinct susceptibility to pathology such as to IL10R deficiency.
source: Despite the known distinct susceptibility of the colon and ileum to pathology, such as to the IL10R deficiency (Glocker et al., 2009; Zigmond et al., 2014)
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citations to prior work.

claim: No comparative analysis of colonic and ileal macrophages has been reported prior to this study.
source: Despite the known distinct susceptibility of the colon and ileum to pathology, such as to the IL10R deficiency (Glocker et al., 2009; Zigmond et al., 2014) and in ulcerative colitis, so far no comparative analysis of their macrophages has been reported.
evidence: This is a statement about the gap in the literature that this study addresses.

claim: Transcriptomes of Ly6C+ BM monocytes and their progeny in colon and ileum displayed 6200 genes differentially expressed at least 2-fold across all analyzed data sets out of a total of 12345 detected genes.
source: Transcriptomes of Ly6C+ BM monocytes, that is the macrophage precursors, and transcriptomes of their progeny in colon and ileum displayed 6200 genes differentially expressed at least 2-fold across all analyzed data sets out of a total of 12345 detected genes (Figure 1—figure supplement 1A–C).
evidence: This is a primary finding based on RNA-seq data analysis, with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: 2255 genes were expressed in monocytes and down-regulated in macrophages (cluster I).
source: 2255 genes were expressed in monocytes and down-regulated in macrophages (cluster I).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Cluster II comprised genes whose expression was absent from monocytes but shared by both small and large intestinal macrophages.
source: Conversely, cluster II comprised genes whose expression was absent from monocytes, but shared by both small and large intestinal macrophages.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: 1087 and 987 genes were either preferentially or exclusively expressed in ileal or colonic macrophages, respectively.
source: Finally, 1087 and 987 genes were either preferentially or exclusively expressed in ileal or colonic macrophages, respectively.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Grafted cells underwent expansion following monocyte transfer.
source: Grafted cells could be visualized in recipient gut tissue and underwent expansion, as reported earlier (Varol et al., 2009) (Figure 1—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is an observation from the experimental system with reference to prior work and supplementary figure.

claim: Graft-derived macrophages were CD11b+ CD64+ Ly6C- and mainly CD11chi.
source: Intestinal tissues of recipient mice were harvested on day 4, 8 and 12 post engraftment (Figure 1A) to isolate graft-derived macrophages according to CD45.1 and CX3CR1/GFP expression; these cells were CD11b+ CD64+ Ly6C- and mainly CD11chi (Figure 1B).
evidence: This is a characterization of the isolated cells based on flow cytometry data shown in Figure 1B.

claim: Transcriptomes of the retrieved engrafted macrophages lacked expression of pro-inflammatory genes such as Saa3, Lcn2, Il1b, Il6 and Tnf, as opposed to cells retrieved from colitic animals treated with DSS.
source: Transcriptomes of the retrieved engrafted macrophages lacked expression of pro-inflammatory genes, such as Saa3, Lcn2, Il1b, Il6 and Tnf, as opposed to cells retrieved from colitic animals treated with Dextran Sulfate Sodium (DSS) (Okayasu et al., 1990) (Figure 1—figure supplement 4).
evidence: This is a finding from transcriptomic analysis comparing engrafted cells to inflammatory controls, with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: The monocyte transfer system mimics cell differentiation close to steady-state conditions.
source: This supports the earlier notion that the cell ablation results in a transient tissue response, but the monocyte transfer system mimics cell differentiation close to steady-state conditions (Varol et al., 2009).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by citation to prior work.

claim: Comparative transcriptome analysis revealed 4213 differentially expressed genes (>4 fold differences in any pairwise comparison among a total of 12878 genes).
source: Comparative transcriptome analysis of grafted monocytes, their progeny retrieved from the recipient intestines, and resident ileal and colonic macrophages that were independently retrieved from Cx3cr1GFP/+ mice revealed 4213 differentially expressed genes (DEG) (>4 fold differences in any pairwise comparison among a total of 12878 genes) (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is a primary finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 1D.

claim: 748 genes were exclusively expressed in the monocyte graft, including Ly6c2, Ccl6 and Cebpe (Cluster I).
source: 748 genes were exclusively expressed in the monocyte graft, including Ly6c2, Ccl6 and Cebpe (Cluster I) (Figure 1D,E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: 793 genes shared expression in graft-derived cells and gut macrophages in colon and ileum (Cluster II), including Irf6, Gata6, Ly6A and Smad7.
source: 793 genes shared expression in graft-derived cells and gut macrophages in colon and ileum (Cluster II). These included Irf6, Gata6, Ly6A and Smad7.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Cluster III comprised 634 genes that were either exclusively or preferentially expressed in colonic macrophages, such as Pparg, Foxa1 and Tlr1.
source: Cluster III comprised 634 genes that were either exclusively or preferentially expressed in colonic macrophages, such as Pparg, Foxa1 and Tlr1 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Cluster IV comprised 539 genes exclusively or preferentially expressed in ileal macrophages, such as Nos2, Sox4 and Mmp9.
source: Cluster IV comprised 539 genes exclusively or preferentially expressed in ileal macrophages, such as Nos2, Sox4 and Mmp9 (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figure.

claim: Genes associated with clusters II, III and IV were associated with distinct pathways, particularly with respect to epithelial cell communication and cell metabolism.
source: Metascape analysis (Zhou et al., 2019) highlighted that genes associated with cluster II, II and IV were associated with distinct pathways, particularly with respect to epithelial cell communication and cell metabolism (Figure 1—figure supplement 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from pathway analysis with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: Early monocyte differentiation (graft vs day 4) was characterized by abundant changes in gene expression in both colon and ileum.
source: Volcano plot analysis revealed that early monocyte differentiation (graft vs day 4) was characterized by abundant changes in gene expression in both colon and ileum.
evidence: This is a finding from the volcano plot analysis of transcriptomic data.

claim: In the colon 3407 genes were up- and 3608 genes were down-regulated from monocytes to day 4.
source: In the colon 3407 genes were up- and 3608 genes were down-regulated; in the ileum 2975 genes were up- and 3206 genes were down-regulated, with up to 10 fold change (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: In the ileum 2975 genes were up- and 3206 genes were down-regulated from monocytes to day 4.
source: In the colon 3407 genes were up- and 3608 genes were down-regulated; in the ileum 2975 genes were up- and 3206 genes were down-regulated, with up to 10 fold change (Figure 1F).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 1F.

claim: Later time points (day 4 to day 8 and day 8 to day 12) were characterized by less pronounced alterations, both with respect to the number of DEG and their fold change.
source: Later time points (day 4 to day 8 and day 8 to day 12) were characterized by less pronounced alterations, both with respect to the number of DEG and their fold change (Figure 1G,H).
evidence: This is a finding from the temporal analysis of transcriptomic data with reference to figures.

claim: In the colon 289 genes (66% of all significantly-changed genes) were induced between day 4 and 8.
source: In the colon 289 genes (66% of all significantly-changed genes) were induced between day 4 and 8 and only 111 genes (19%) were up-regulated between day 8 and 12.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the temporal transcriptomic analysis.

claim: In the colon only 111 genes (19%) were up-regulated between day 8 and 12.
source: In the colon 289 genes (66% of all significantly-changed genes) were induced between day 4 and 8 and only 111 genes (19%) were up-regulated between day 8 and 12.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the temporal transcriptomic analysis.

claim: In the ileum 95 genes (21%) were up-regulated between day 4 and 8.
source: In the ileum this trend was reversed, with 95 genes (21%) up-regulated between day 4 and 8, but 321 genes (85%) induced between day 8 and 12.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the temporal transcriptomic analysis.

claim: In the ileum 321 genes (85%) were induced between day 8 and 12.
source: In the ileum this trend was reversed, with 95 genes (21%) up-regulated between day 4 and 8, but 321 genes (85%) induced between day 8 and 12.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the temporal transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Monocytes that enter distinct gut segments rapidly acquire characteristic transcriptomic signatures.
source: Collectively, this establishes that monocytes that enter distinct gut segments rapidly acquire characteristic transcriptomic signatures.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transcriptomic data showing early and tissue-specific gene expression changes.

claim: Even by day 12, monocyte graft-derived cells differed in expression profiles when compared to resident ileal and colonic macrophages.
source: Interestingly, even by day 12, monocyte graft-derived cells differed in expression profiles when compared to resident ileal and colonic macrophages (Figure 2A).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic comparison with reference to Figure 2A.

claim: Differences between engrafted and resident macrophages might be attributable to incomplete macrophage maturation or to the recently reported heterogeneity of the intestinal macrophage compartment.
source: These differences might be attributable to incomplete macrophage maturation or to the recently reported heterogeneity of the intestinal macrophage compartment (Shaw et al., 2018; De Schepper et al., 2018).
evidence: This is a speculative interpretation of the observed differences with citations to relevant work.

claim: The majority of the cells retrieved likely comprise lamina propria/mucosa resident macrophages, rather than the less abundant macrophages of the submucosa or muscularis layer.
source: Notably, the majority of the cells we retrieve likely comprise lamina propria/mucosa resident macrophages, rather than the less abundant macrophages of the submucosa or muscularis layer (Shaw et al., 2018; De Schepper et al., 2018).
evidence: This is an inference about the cell population being studied based on the isolation method and cited work.

claim: Generation of a CD4+ Timd4+ subpopulation of lamina propria macrophages was reported to require prolonged residence in the tissue.
source: Generation of a CD4+ Timd4+ subpopulation of lamina propria macrophages was reported to require prolonged residence in the tissue (Shaw et al., 2018).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Grafted cells in both colon and ileum acquired with time some expression of Timd4 (Tim4).
source: Although grafted cells in both colon and ileum acquired with time some expression of a hallmark of the long-lived cells, the phosphatidyl serine receptor Timd4 (Tim4) (Figure 2B, Figure 1D cluster VI)
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Signature genes of long-lived macrophages such as Cd209f, C2 and Rusc2 were not expressed in engrafted cells in the time frame analyzed.
source: Although grafted cells in both colon and ileum acquired with time some expression of a hallmark of the long-lived cells, the phosphatidyl serine receptor Timd4 (Tim4) (Figure 2B, Figure 1D cluster VI), other signature genes, such as Cd209f, C2 and Rusc2 (Shaw et al., 2018), were not expressed in the time frame analyzed here (Figure 2B).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures and cited work.

claim: The hypothesis that 12 days were insufficient for engrafted macrophages to acquire the full gene expression profile of resident cells was corroborated by the delayed onset of MHCII (encoded by H2-ab1) expression.
source: The hypothesis that 12 days were insufficient for engrafted macrophages to acquire the full gene expression profile of resident cells was furthermore corroborated by the delayed onset of MHCII (encoded by H2-ab1) expression, one of the markers for intestinal macrophage maturation (Tamoutounour et al., 2012; Schridde et al., 2017) (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is an interpretation of the data supported by citations to prior work and reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Engrafted macrophages were characterized by lack of expression of Irf1 and the TAM receptor kinase family member Axl.
source: Engrafted macrophages were also characterized by lack of expression of Irf1 and the member of the TAM receptor kinase family Axl (Figure 2C).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 2C.

claim: Genes encoding ribosome-associated proteins and histones were low to absent in resident macrophages from both colon and ileum but prominent in the engrafted cells.
source: Genes, whose expression was low to absent in resident macrophages from both colon and ileum, but prominent in the engrafted cells (Figure 1D cluster VII), included the ones encoding ribosome-associated proteins and histones (Figure 2D).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The reconstitution of emptied intestinal tissue with monocyte-derived cells involves clonal expansion.
source: As previously shown (Varol et al., 2009), the reconstitution of emptied intestinal tissue with monocyte-derived cells involves clonal expansion, that is less likely to occur in physiological setting.
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work.

claim: Out of the 6383 genes significantly differing between engrafted and resident macrophages from either colon or ileum, 897 were annotated with a Gene Ontology (GO) term associated with 'proliferation' and 'cell cycle'.
source: In line with this notion, out of the 6383 genes significantly differing between engrafted and resident macrophages from either colon or ileum, 897 were annotated with a Gene Ontology (GO) term associated with 'proliferation' and 'cell cycle'
evidence: This is a finding from the GO term analysis of differentially expressed genes.

claim: Il10ra was not induced in engrafted colonic macrophages even 12 days after tissue entry.
source: Interestingly, Il10ra was not induced in engrafted colonic macrophages, even 12 days after tissue entry, while engrafted ileal macrophages displayed Il10ra transcripts as early as day 4 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: Engrafted ileal macrophages displayed Il10ra transcripts as early as day 4.
source: Interestingly, Il10ra was not induced in engrafted colonic macrophages, even 12 days after tissue entry, while engrafted ileal macrophages displayed Il10ra transcripts as early as day 4 (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: Expression of the cytokine IL10 itself was almost absent from monocytes and engrafted macrophages in both tissues but significantly present in resident macrophages retrieved from non-engrafted Cx3cr1GFP/+ mice, to a larger extent in the colon than the ileum.
source: Expression of the cytokine IL10 itself was almost absent from monocytes and engrafted macrophages in both tissues, but significantly present in resident macrophages retrieved from non-engrafted Cx3cr1GFP/+ mice, to a larger extent in the colon than the ileum (Figure 2E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 2E.

claim: Il1b expression displayed a similar pattern to Il10 in line with an earlier suggestion that IL1 might induce macrophage IL-10 expression.
source: Of note, Il1b expression displayed a similar pattern in line with an earlier suggestion that IL1 might induce macrophage IL-10 expression (Foey et al., 1998).
evidence: This is an observation from the data interpreted in light of cited prior work.

claim: Genes induced following macrophage exposure to Il10, such as Ccr5 and Socs3, displayed similar expression patterns to Il10.
source: Likewise, genes induced following macrophage exposure to Il10, such as Ccr5 (Houle et al., 1999) and Socs3 (Cassatella et al., 1999) displayed similar expression patterns.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis interpreted in light of cited prior work.

claim: In the experimental model, the IL10/IL10R axis is inactive in newly differentiated macrophages and established only after further maturation in the tissue.
source: This suggests that in our model the IL10/IL10R axis is inactive in newly differentiated macrophages and established only after further maturation in the tissue.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transcriptomic data regarding IL10 and IL10R expression patterns.

claim: Flow cytometric analysis of colon tissue of WT C57BL/6 mice identifies a small population of CD11b+ Ly6C+ MHCII- cells that likely represent recent monocyte immigrants into the tissue.
source: Flow cytometric analysis of colon tissue of WT C57BL/6 mice identifies a small population of CD11b+ Ly6C+ MHCII- cells that likely represent recent monocyte immigrants into the tissue (Figure 2—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is a finding from flow cytometry with reference to supplementary figure and an inference about cell identity.

claim: Endogenous gut immigrants down-regulated monocyte markers and gained a gut macrophage signature, including expression of FoxD2 and Nr3c2.
source: Global RNAseq analysis of this population, alongside the Ly6C+ MHCII- macrophages revealed that, like the day four graft, these endogenous gut immigrants down-regulated monocyte markers and gained a gut macrophage signature, including expression of the Forkhead transcription factor (TF) FoxD2 and the nuclear receptor Nr3c2 (Figure 2—figure supplement 1B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to supplementary figures.

claim: Endogenous gut immigrants did not display a signature indicating proliferation, such as Rpl10 or Hmga1.
source: Endogenous gut immigrants did not display a signature indicating proliferation, such as Rpl10 or Hmga1.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Early colonic immigrants lacked signature genes associated with long-lived gut macrophages, including Timd4 and CD209f, as well as expression of Il10ra and Il10.
source: However, like the grafted cells, these early colonic immigrants lacked signature genes associated with long-lived gut macrophages, including Timd4 and CD209f, as well as expression of Il10ra and Il10.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: The gene lists of upregulated and down regulated genes in macrophages retrieved from engrafted [CD11c-DTR > WT] and [CX3CR1-DTR > WT] chimeras showed with 71% and 59%, respectively, considerable overlap.
source: The gene lists of upregulated and down regulated genes in macrophages retrieved from engrafted [CD11c-DTR > WT] and [CX3CR1-DTR > WT] chimeras showed with 71% and 59%, respectively, considerable overlap (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative analysis of two different experimental models with reference to supplementary figure.

claim: Despite some differences, monocyte graft-derived cells recapitulate the 'monocyte waterfall'.
source: Collectively, these data show that despite some differences, monocyte graft-derived cells recapitulate the 'monocyte waterfall' (Tamoutounour et al., 2012).
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the data with citation to the original description of the monocyte waterfall.

claim: 458 genes were up-regulated during monocyte differentiation in a segment-specific manner – 351 in colonic macrophages and 107 in ileal macrophages.
source: 458 genes were up-regulated during monocyte differentiation in a segment-specific manner – 351 in colonic macrophages and 107 in ileal macrophages (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Monocyte differentiation into ileal macrophages was accompanied by induction of Gata and Hbox TF family members, such as Gata5 and Hbox3.
source: Monocyte differentiation into ileal macrophages was accompanied by induction of Gata and Hbox TF family members, such as Gata5 and Hbox3 (Figure 3A)
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Monocyte differentiation into ileal macrophages was accompanied by induction of genes encoding the chemokine Ccl5 and the chemokine receptor CCR9.
source: Monocyte differentiation into ileal macrophages was accompanied by induction of Gata and Hbox TF family members, such as Gata5 and Hbox3 (Figure 3A), as well as genes encoding the chemokine Ccl5 and the chemokine receptor CCR9.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Monocytes that entered colon tissue preferentially up-regulated Foxd2, the nuclear receptor Nr3c2, and the dominant negative helix-loop-helix protein Id2.
source: Monocytes that entered colon tissue preferentially up-regulated Foxd2, the nuclear receptor Nr3c2, and the dominant negative helix-loop-helix protein Id2 (Figure 3A).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3A.

claim: Of the genes specifically down-regulated in only one intestinal segment, 78 genes followed this trend in colonic and 99 in ileal macrophages.
source: Of the genes, which were specifically down-regulated in only one intestinal segment, 78 genes followed this trend in colonic and 99 in ileal macrophages.
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Genes specifically down-regulated in ileal macrophages included 7 TFs, such as Foxp1 and Trim16.
source: The latter down-regulated genes included 7 TFs, such as Foxp1 and Trim16, while Arid5a and Elk3 were specifically down-regulated in the colon (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Arid5a and Elk3 were specifically down-regulated in the colon.
source: The latter down-regulated genes included 7 TFs, such as Foxp1 and Trim16, while Arid5a and Elk3 were specifically down-regulated in the colon (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3B.

claim: Many genes related to immune reaction and response to challenge displayed higher expression in ileal macrophages than their colonic counterparts.
source: Many genes related to immune reaction and response to challenge displayed higher expression in ileal macrophages than their colonic counterparts.
evidence: This is a general observation from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Arid5a, whose gene product regulates IL6, is down-regulated in colonic macrophages.
source: Examples are: Arid5a, whose gene product regulates IL6 (Masuda et al., 2016)
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work on gene function.

claim: Elk3, which encodes a member of the ETS TF family and was reported to modulate the phagocytosis of bacteria by macrophages, is down-regulated in colonic macrophages.
source: Elk3, which encodes a member of the ETS TF family and was reported to modulate the phagocytosis of bacteria by macrophages (Tsoyi et al., 2015)
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work on gene function.

claim: Ano6, which is down-regulated in colonic macrophages, reportedly supports microbiocidal activity of macrophages involving P2X7 receptor signaling.
source: and Ano6, that is down-regulated in colonic macrophages (Figure 3B), and reportedly supports microbiocidal activity of macrophages involving P2X7 receptor signaling (Ousingsawat et al., 2015).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work on gene function and reference to Figure 3B.

claim: The enzyme Sod1, which was reported to impair macrophage-related parasite killing in cutaneous Leishmaniasis, showed lower expression in ileal macrophages.
source: In contrast, the enzyme Sod1, which was reported to impair macrophage-related parasite killing in cutaneous Leishmaniasis (Khouri et al., 2009), showed lower expression in ileal macrophages (Figure 3B).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work on gene function and reference to Figure 3B.

claim: 54 genes were expressed in colonic engrafted macrophages and silenced in their ileal counterparts.
source: 54 such genes were expressed in colonic engrafted macrophages and silenced in their ileal counterparts; 15 genes followed an opposite trend (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: 15 genes were expressed in ileal engrafted macrophages and silenced in their colonic counterparts.
source: 54 such genes were expressed in colonic engrafted macrophages and silenced in their ileal counterparts; 15 genes followed an opposite trend (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: KLF4 was the only TF found in both groups of genes that are up-regulated in one tissue and down-regulated in the other.
source: Only one TF was found in both groups, KLF4 (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Aldh2 encoded by Aldh2 was recently reported to play a role in repression of ATP6V0E2, which is critical for proper lysosomal function, autophagy, and degradation of oxidized LDL.
source: Aldh2 encoded by Aldh2, mostly known for its role in alcohol detoxification, was recently reported to play a role in repression of ATP6V0E2, which is critical for proper lysosomal function, autophagy, and degradation of oxidized LDL (Zhong et al., 2019) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as recent knowledge with citation to prior work and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Hdac7 encoded by Hdac7 and up-regulated in ileal macrophages and down-regulated in colonic macrophages was reported to interfere with the myeloid gene expression pattern and to inhibit macrophage-specific functions.
source: Hdac7 encoded by Hdac7 and up-regulated in ileal macrophages and down-regulated in colonic macrophages, was reported to interfere with the myeloid gene expression pattern and to inhibited macrophage-specific functions (Barneda-Zahonero et al., 2013) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work on gene function and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Fmnl3 participates in filopodia generation.
source: Finally, Fmnl3 participates in filopodia generation (Harris et al., 2010) (Figure 3C).
evidence: This is stated as established knowledge with citation to prior work and reference to Figure 3C.

claim: Monocytes establish gut segment specific gene expression patterns, likely under the influence of local cues.
source: Collectively, these data establish that monocytes establish gut segment specific gene expression patterns, likely under the influence of local cues.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the transcriptomic data showing segment-specific gene expression.

claim: By day 4, expression of 2007 genes was down-regulated more than 2-fold in the monocyte graft following differentiation into macrophages in both tissues (out of 12485 genes expressed).
source: Overall, by day 4, expression of 2007 genes was down-regulated more than 2-fold in the monocyte graft following differentiation into macrophages in both tissues (out of 12485 genes expressed).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: 2404 genes were induced in both the colon and ileum by day 4, arguably as part of a generic transcriptome signature of intestinal macrophages.
source: 2404 genes were induced in both the colon and ileum, arguably as part of a generic transcriptome signature of intestinal macrophages (Figure 4A).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 4A and an interpretation.

claim: 919 of the genes induced during monocyte differentiation into generic intestinal macrophages displayed very low prior expression in monocytes – below 50 reads.
source: Notably, 919 of the genes induced during monocyte differentiation into generic intestinal macrophages displayed very low prior expression in monocytes – below 50 reads (Figure 4B).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Expression of 183 transcripts seemed to be actively silenced during the differentiation process.
source: In contrast, expression of fewer transcripts (183) seemed to be actively silenced during the differentiation process, as seen in the violin blot in Figure 4B.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 4B.

claim: Monocytes actively acquire macrophage identities by de novo mRNA synthesis, while much of the monocytic gene expression is compatible with the differentiation process.
source: This implies that monocytes actively acquire macrophage identities by de novo mRNA synthesis, while much of the monocytic gene expression is compatible with the differentiation process.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the transcriptomic data regarding gene induction versus silencing.

claim: The top 5 GO-terms associated with genes up-regulated in intestinal macrophages related to cell adhesion and migration processes.
source: The top 5 GO-terms associated with genes up-regulated in intestinal macrophages related to cell adhesion and migration processes (Figure 4C)
evidence: This is a finding from the GO term analysis with reference to Figure 4C.

claim: The top 5 GO-terms associated with down-regulated genes in macrophages included cell cycle and division, as well as mRNA processing and DNA repair.
source: The top 5 GO-terms associated with down-regulated genes in macrophages included cell cycle and division, as well as mRNA processing and DNA repair (Figure 4C,D)
evidence: This is a finding from the GO term analysis with reference to figures.

claim: The data are in line with the transformation of circulating monocytes into non-migratory tissue resident cells.
source: Collectively, these data are in line with the transformation of circulating monocytes into non-migratory tissue resident cells and suggest a role for DNA damage-associated molecules during the differentiation process.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GO term analysis results.

claim: The data suggest a role for DNA damage-associated molecules during the differentiation process.
source: Collectively, these data are in line with the transformation of circulating monocytes into non-migratory tissue resident cells and suggest a role for DNA damage-associated molecules during the differentiation process.
evidence: This is an interpretation of the GO term analysis results.

claim: Four of the Cebp family members (Cebpa, b, d, g) were significantly down-regulated upon monocyte differentiation into macrophages.
source: Four of the Cebp family members (Cebpa, b, d, g) and 5 E2F family members (E2f2, 4, 6, 7, 8) were significantly down-regulated upon monocyte differentiation into macrophages (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: 5 E2F family members (E2f2, 4, 6, 7, 8) were significantly down-regulated upon monocyte differentiation into macrophages.
source: Four of the Cebp family members (Cebpa, b, d, g) and 5 E2F family members (E2f2, 4, 6, 7, 8) were significantly down-regulated upon monocyte differentiation into macrophages (Figure 5A).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 5A.

claim: Egr1, 2 and 3 were up-regulated upon monocyte differentiation into macrophages.
source: In contrast, Egr1, 2 and 3 were up-regulated.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Down-regulated TFs included the regulators of immune response Bach1, Bcl6, Irf9, Nfatc3, Nfkb1 and Rela, as well as the master macrophage TF Spi1 (PU.1).
source: Other down-regulated TFs included the regulators of immune response Bach1, Bcl6, Irf9, Nfatc3, Nfkb1 and Rela, as well as the master macrophage TF Spi1 (PU.1) (Figure 5B).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 5B.

claim: The list of induced genes was enriched with homeobox TFs such as Sox13, Pbx1, Foxa1 and others.
source: The list of induced genes was enriched with homeobox TFs such as Sox13, Pbx1, Foxa1 and others (Figure 5C).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 5C.

claim: The induced genes group comprised TFs that had previously been reported to be critical for the development of other tissue macrophages, such as the nuclear receptor LXRα encoded by Nr1h3 for splenic macrophages and Gata6 for peritoneal macrophages.
source: In addition, this group comprised TFs that had previously been reported to be critical for the development of other tissue macrophages, such as the nuclear receptor LXRα encoded by Nr1h3 for splenic macrophages and Gata6 for peritoneal macrophages (Varol et al., 2015; Rosas et al., 2014).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis interpreted in light of cited prior work.

claim: Vasculature-resident Ly6C- monocytes and gut macrophages that derive both from Ly6C+ monocytes display considerable overlap in transcriptomic signatures.
source: Collectively, these data establish that vasculature-resident Ly6C- monocytes and gut macrophages that derive both from Ly6C+ monocytes display considerable overlap in transcriptomic signatures, but also display gene expression patterns that are likely associated with their specific environments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Vasculature-resident Ly6C- monocytes and gut macrophages display gene expression patterns that are likely associated with their specific environments.
source: Collectively, these data establish that vasculature-resident Ly6C- monocytes and gut macrophages that derive both from Ly6C+ monocytes display considerable overlap in transcriptomic signatures, but also display gene expression patterns that are likely associated with their specific environments.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Monocyte progeny in vasculature and tissue shared signatures showing considerable similarities as reflected in the expression pattern of two thirds of the genes (66.7%).
source: Monocyte progeny, whether in vasculature or tissue shared signatures, showed considerable similarities as reflected in the expression pattern of two thirds of the genes (66.7%).
evidence: This is a quantitative finding from the comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Clusters I and II comprised 780 genes that were down-regulated upon Ly6C+ monocyte differentiation, including hallmark monocyte markers such as Ly6c, Ccr2 and Mmp8 and Myd88.
source: Specifically, clusters I and II comprised 780 genes that were down-regulated upon Ly6C+ monocyte differentiation, including hallmark monocyte markers, such as Ly6c, Ccr2 and Mmp8 and Myd88 (Figure 6B,C).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: 160 genes were induced in both blood- and tissue resident monocyte-derived cells, albeit to different extent, including Pparg, Ets2 and Tgfbr2 (Cluster III).
source: 160 genes were induced in both blood- and tissue resident monocyte-derived cells, albeit to different extend, including as Pparg, Ets2 and Tgfbr2 (Cluster III) (Figure 6B,D).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative transcriptomic analysis with reference to figures.

claim: Cluster IV comprised 253 genes up-regulated in blood-resident cells and down-regulated in gut macrophages, including Csf2ra, Nfkb1, Il10ra and Spi1 (PU.1).
source: Specifically, cluster IV comprised 253 genes up-regulated in blood-resident cells and down-regulated in gut macrophages. This included Csf2ra, Nfkb1, Il10ra and Spi1 (PU.1).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Cluster V comprised 110 genes induced in gut macrophages but not vasculature-resident cells, such as the mitochondrial master regulator Ppargc1b and the metalloprotease Adam19.
source: Cluster V comprised 110 genes induced in gut macrophages but not vasculature-resident cells, such as the mitochondrial master regulator Ppargc1b and the metalloprotease Adam19 (Figure 6B).
evidence: This is a finding from the comparative transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 6B.

claim: Cebpb was induced in Ly6C- blood monocytes, as was previously reported.
source: Concerning TFs, Cebpb was induced in Ly6C- blood monocytes, as was previously reported (Mildner et al., 2017)
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with citation to prior work.

claim: Cebpa and Cebpd were down-regulated in both blood- and gut-resident cells.
source: Concerning TFs, Cebpb was induced in Ly6C- blood monocytes, as was previously reported (Mildner et al., 2017), while Cebpa and Cebpd were down-regulated in both blood- and gut-resident cells (Figure 6E).
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis with reference to Figure 6E.

claim: Irf family members 7, 8 and 9 were down-regulated during Ly6C+ monocyte differentiation in blood and gut.
source: Irf family members 7, 8 and 9 were down-regulated during Ly6C+ monocyte differentiation in blood and gut.
evidence: This is a finding from the transcriptomic analysis.

claim: Tissue-specific macrophage imprinting occurs early during development, shortly after tissue infiltration.
source: Tissue-specific macrophage imprinting occurs hence early during development, shortly after tissue infiltration.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the observation that engrafted cells segregate by tissue at day 4.

claim: Two samples of engrafted ileal macrophages clustered with the colonic samples rather than the ileal ones, suggesting that the colonic signature is default.
source: Interestingly, two samples of engrafted ileal macrophages clustered with the colonic samples rather than the ileal ones, suggesting that the colonic signature is default.
evidence: This is an observation from the clustering analysis and an interpretation.

claim: Colonic macrophages at day 12 post engraftment were more distinct from endogenous colonic macrophages compared to their ileal counterparts, which implies that the mature colonic gene signature might take longer time to develop or could be more heterogeneous.
source: Colonic macrophages at day 12 post engraftment were also more distinct from endogenous colonic macrophages, compared to their ileal counterparts, which implies that the mature colonic gene signature might take longer time to develop or could be more heterogeneous.
evidence: This is an observation from the transcriptomic comparison and a speculative interpretation.

claim: The majority of changes in gene expression, both in fold change and numbers, occurred in the transition from monocytes to either colonic or ileal macrophages at day four post transfer.
source: The majority of changes in gene expression, both in fold change and numbers, occurred in the transition from monocytes to either colonic or ileal macrophages at day four post transfer, that is immediately after extravasation.
evidence: This is a conclusion drawn from the temporal transcriptomic analysis.

claim: The data sets can provide a starting point for hypothesis-driven experiments.
source: Together with earlier reports (Mildner et al., 2017; Schridde et al., 2017), our data sets can provide a starting point for hypothesis-driven experiments.
evidence: This is a statement about the utility of the data generated in this study.
